title: Cone model comparison after the ordinary-base target change
statement: Use simplicial sets, ordinary nerves, coherent realization, ordered cone pushouts and enriched diagrams as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], [lem-coef-unmarked-straightening-quillen], [lem-coef-simplicial-right-fibration-presentation], [lem-coef-unmarked-straightening-target-change], [lem-coef-enriched-diagram-rectification], [lem-coef-simplicial-projective-model-calculus] and [lem-coef-simplicial-presheaf-projective-model]. Let $C$ be a small ordinary category, $B=N(C)$, $S=B^{\mathrm{op}}$, let $X\to B$ be any simplicial map, and let $D:C\to\mathsf{Kan}_{\mathcal U}$ be a strict Kan-valued diagram. Put $A=\mathfrak C[S]^{\mathrm{op}}\cong\mathfrak C[B]$, let $u:A\to C$ be the opposite coherent-nerve counit, and let $P=T_S(X^{\mathrm{op}})$ be the ordered-cone diagram of [lem-coef-simplicial-right-fibration-presentation]. Then $u$ is a Dwyer--Kan equivalence, $P$ is projectively cofibrant, and the target-change isomorphism identifies $u_!P$ naturally with the cone diagram $H_C(X)$. If $w:u_!P\to D^{\mathrm{op}}$ is an objectwise weak homotopy equivalence, its enriched Kan-extension adjoint $P\to u^*D^{\mathrm{op}}$ is an objectwise weak equivalence; the cone Quillen-equivalence criterion then gives a contravariant weak equivalence $X^{\mathrm{op}}\to U_S(u^*D^{\mathrm{op}})$ and, after taking opposites, a covariant weak equivalence $X\to U_B^{\mathrm{cov}}(u^*D^{\mathrm{op}})$. All these maps are natural in $X$ and in maps of strict Kan diagrams.

source.place: Remark 3.2.5.10 and Lemma 3.2.5.17(1), Proposition 3.2.5.18(1), together with the enriched projective Quillen criterion and the ordinary covariant presentation
